blocks.name: ADC
blocks.maskDescription:
Configures the Type 3 to Type 5 ADC to output data collected from the ADC pins on the processor.
SOC: Start of Conversion
EOC: End of Conversion

blocks.name: AnalogIO Input
blocks.maskDescription: Configures AIO inputs for the specified pins with qualification type settings.

blocks.name: AnalogIO Output
blocks.maskDescription:
Configures AIO outputs for the specified pins.
In regular mode a value of True at the input of the block will pull the AIO pin high. A value of False will ground the pin. In toggle mode, a value of True at the input of the block will switch the actual output level of the AIO pin. A value of False has no effect on the output level of the AIO pin.

blocks.name: COMP

blocks.name: ePWM

The number of available ePWM modules vary between C2000 processors.

blocks.name: LIN Transmit
blocks.maskDescription: Configures the C2803x LIN port to transmit messages to the Local Interconnect Network (LIN).

blocks.name: ADC
blocks.maskDescription: Configures the ADC to output a constant stream of data collected from the ADC pins on the C280x/C2833x DSP.

blocks.name: CAN Receive
blocks.maskDescription:
Configures a CAN mailbox to receive messages from the CAN bus pins on the C28x DSP. When the message is received, emits the function call to the connected function-call subsystem as well as outputs the message data in the selected format and the message data length in bytes. 
CAN_B module is only available on certain C2000 processors.

The block supports eCAN or DCAN depending upon the type of C2000 processors.

blocks.name: CAN Transmit
blocks.maskDescription:
Configures a CAN mailbox to transmit messages to the CAN bus pins on the C28x DSP. 
CAN_B module is only available on certain C2000 processors.

The block supports eCAN or DCAN depending upon the type of C2000 processors.

blocks.name: I2C Receive
blocks.maskDescription: Configures the I2C module to receive data from the I2C bus.

blocks.name: I2C Transmit
blocks.maskDescription: Configures the I2C module to transmit data on the I2C bus.

blocks.name: SCI Receive
blocks.maskDescription: Configures Serial Communication Interface (SCI) of the C2000 MCUs to receive data from SCIRXD pin. This enables asynchronous serial digital communications between the MCU and other connected peripherals.

blocks.name: SCI Transmit
blocks.maskDescription: Configures Serial Communication Interface (SCI) of the C2000 MCUs to transmit data via SCITXD pin. This enables asynchronous serial digital communications between the MCU and other connected peripherals.

blocks.name: Software Interrupt Trigger
blocks.maskDescription:
Triggers a hardware interrupt in software.
Use this block to trigger any interrupt line available in the on-chip PIE controller.
Use this block in combination with the Hardware Interrupt block to react on the triggered interrupt.

blocks.name: Watchdog
blocks.maskDescription: Configures the Watchdog module on the DSP.

blocks.name: eCAP
blocks.maskDescription:
Configure the settings of the Enhanced Capture (eCAP) for C28x / C29x processors. 
The block output can be in 'HRCLK / SYSCLK cycles' or in 'Microseconds' where HRCLK is for high resolution mode and SYSCLK is for the normal mode. Time-Stamp counter data type should be 'single' or 'double' for output in 'Microseconds' else you may encounter data loss.

blocks.name: ePWM
blocks.maskDescription: Configures the Event Manager of the C280x/C2833x DSP to generate ePWM waveforms.

blocks.name: eQEP
blocks.maskDescription:
The enhanced quadrature encoder pulse (eQEP) module is used for direct interface with a linear or rotary incremental encoder to get position, direction, and speed information from a rotating machine for use in a high-performance motion and position-control system.
The eQEP inputs include two pins for quadrature-clock mode or direction-count mode, an index (or 0 marker), and a strobe input.

blocks.name: QEP
blocks.maskDescription: Configures quadrature encoder pulse circuit associated with the selected Event Manager module to decode and count quadrature encoded pulses applied to related input pins (QEP1 and QEP2 for EVA or QEP3 and QEP4 for EVB). Depending on the selected counting mode, the output is either the pulse count or the rotor speed (when a pulse signal comes from an optical encoder mounted on a rotating machine).

CLA Math functions include trigonometric, logarithmic, exponential and power functions. 
Trigonometric functions accept input in radians. 
PU Trigonometric functions accept input in per unit. 
The block accepts only input of datatype single and outputs data of type single.

blocks.name: Hardware Interrupt
blocks.maskDescription:
Trigger the downstream function-call subsystem from an interrupt service routine.

The block outputs trigger the downstream connected function-call subsystems when the selected interrupt occurs.

Select the interrupt service routine with the 'Interrupt group' and the 'Interrupt name' parameters.
Select events and respective events execution order from 'Events to serve' group to service events from selected 'Interrupt name'.
Use the 'Simulink task priority' parameter to set the priority of the downstream function-call subsystem.
Enable 'Run interrupt service routine as atomic unit' to block all other interrupts while executing the selected interrupt service routine.
Enable 'Clear status after servicing each event' to clear event status in interrupt service routine after executing each event.

blocks.name: Absolute IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block computes the absolute value of an IQ number. Both the input and the output are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers. The respective IQNabs function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: Arctangent IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block computes the 4-quadrant arctangent for two IQ numbers given in the same Q format. All inputs and outputs are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers. Depending on the selected option, the output of the block is either in radians and varies from -pi to +pi or in per unit (PU) and varies from 0 to 1. The respective IQNatan function is selected by the input data type.

blocks.name: Float to IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block converts a floating-point input to the equivalent IQ value. The input is a single-precission floating-point number and the output is a signed 32-bit fixed-point number. The respective IQN function is selected based on the Q value specified for the output.

blocks.name: Fractional part IQN x int32
blocks.maskDescription: This block multiplies an IQ number with a long integer number and returns the fractional part of the result. First input and the output are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers, while the second input is a long integer number. The respective IQNmpyI32frac function is selected based on the Q value of the input.

blocks.name: Fractional part IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block returns the fractional part of an IQ number. Both the input and output are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers. The respective IQNfrac function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: IQN / IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block divides two IQN numbers using Newton-Raphson technique. All inputs and outputs are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers that have the same Q value. The respective IQNdiv function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: IQN to Float
blocks.maskDescription: This block converts an IQ number to the equivalent floating-point value in IEEE 754 format. The input is a signed 32-bit fixed-point number and the output is a single-precission floating-point number. The respective IQNtoF function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: IQN x IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block multiplies two IQ numbers that are represented in same IQ format. Depending on the multiplication option selected below, the result can also be rounded or saturated. All inputs and outputs are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers. The respective IQNmpy function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: IQN x int32
blocks.maskDescription: This block multiplies an IQ number with a long integer. First input and the output are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers, while the second input is a long integer number. The respective IQNmpyI32 function is selected based on the Q value of the first input.

blocks.name: IQN1 to IQN2
blocks.maskDescription: This block converts an IQ number to a new IQ number in specified Q format. Both the input and output are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers. The respective IQNtoIQx function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: IQN1 x IQN2
blocks.maskDescription: This block multiplies two IQ numbers that are represented in different IQ format. All inputs and outputs are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers. The respective IQNmpyIQX function is selected based on the Q value specified for the output.

blocks.name: Integer part IQN x int32
blocks.maskDescription: This block multiplies an IQ number with a long integer number and returns the integer part of the result. First input is a signed 32-bit fixed-point number, while the second input and the output are long integer numbers. The respective IQNmpyI32int function is selected based on the Q value of the input.

blocks.name: Integer part IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block returns the integer part of an IQ number. The input is a signed 32-bit fixed-point number and the output is a long integer number. The respective IQNint function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: Magnitude IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block computes the magnitude of two IQ numbers. All inputs and outputs are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers in the same Q format. The respective IQNmag function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: Saturate IQN
blocks.maskDescription:
This block saturates the value of an IQ number to the given upper and lower limits. Both the input and the output are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers. The respective IQsat function is selected based on the Q value.
The upper and lower limits have to be given as real world values.

blocks.name: Square Root IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block computes the square root and the inverse square root of an IQ number using table lookup and Newton-Raphson approximation. Both the input and the output are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers. The respective IQNsqrt function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: Trig Fcn IQN
blocks.maskDescription: This block computes selected trigonometric functions of an IQ number. Both the input and the output are signed 32-bit fixed-point numbers. The respective trigonometric function is selected based on the Q value.

blocks.name: C28x Hardware Interrupt
blocks.maskDescription:
Create Interrupt Service Routine which will execute the downstream subsystem.

Note: The default model base sample rate priority is set to 40 with a lower priority value indicating a higher priority task. These parameters can be changed in the 'Solver' pane of the 'Configuration Parameters'. The Simulink task priority of the selected interrupt is relative to the model base rate priority settings.

blocks.name: Hardware Profiler
blocks.maskDescription:
Profiles functions using GPIO, ERAD or Timer measurement modes.

GPIO: Selected pin is set and cleared before and after the execution of the downstream function-call subsystem.
ERAD: The duration between the start and end of execution of the downstream function-call subsystem is measured.
Timer: Timer 2 count is read before and after the execution of the downstream function-call subsystem. The difference between these timer reads is computed.
